requirements.text: increase the impact of the incident to high
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM incident WHERE incident_id = 'INC_003' AND impact = 'high' AND priority = 'high'
requirements.source: Verify if the priority of the incident is set correctly.
assumptions: two seed rows carry number INC0000003 (INC_003 in ORG_001, INC_010 in ORG_002); the request's 'printer connectivity issue' is INC_003's short_description
priority follows the policy 3.1 matrix: impact high x urgency medium (seed value, unchanged by the request) = high
'the necessary details' read as the priority and the SLA alignment that policy 3.1 and 6 derive from impact; no work note is asked for and no tool writes one

requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM incident_sla WHERE incident_sla_id = 'TSLA_011' AND incident_id = 'INC_003' AND sla_def_id = 'SLA_002'
requirements.source: Verify if the correct high-priority SLA is linked to the incident.
assumptions: id assumed next in sequence (TSLA_011 after TSLA_010)
policy 6: SLAs align to priority; SLA_002 is the only active sla_definition with applies_to_priority = high in the incident's org ORG_001 (SLA_008 is ORG_002's)
the existing link TSLA_004 (SLA_001, completed) is left alone: nothing in the request or policy asks for its removal, and no tool updates incident_sla rows
the anchor is stricter than the original check, which has no id: if the server numbers incident_sla rows differently from TSLA_011 the anchor, not the SLA choice, is what fails

requirements.text: incident INC0000003 (the printer connectivity issue, not the other row with that number)
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM incident WHERE incident_id = 'INC_010' AND impact = 'medium' AND urgency = 'low' AND priority = 'moderate'
assumptions: selector boundary: INC_010 ('Server maintenance request', ORG_002) also carries number INC0000003 and must not be the row raised
disagreement: cells: A tests impact, urgency and priority, B tests impact and priority; kept A's tighter set because both hold on the seed and the priority matrix reads all three

requirements.text: incident INC0000003 (the printer connectivity issue, not the other row with that number)
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM incident_sla WHERE incident_id = 'INC_010'
assumptions: selector boundary: no SLA may be linked to the other INC0000003 row; its one seed link (TSLA_008) stays
disagreement: only A wrote this; kept because it is the same selector boundary (the second INC0000003 row) applied to the table the SLA link is written to

requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM incident_sla WHERE incident_id = 'INC_003' AND sla_def_id = 'SLA_008'
assumptions: selector boundary: SLA_008 shares the name 'High Priority Resolution SLA' with SLA_002 but belongs to ORG_002, not the incident's org

notes:
Merged from two independent passes that agree on both dispositions and on every value. disagreement: A's stay that INC_010 (the other INC0000003 row) keeps its one SLA link (B had no such requirement); kept because it is the same selector boundary as the INC_010 incident stay both passes wrote, applied to the table the SLA link is written to. disagreement: form: the INC_010 incident stay tests three cells in A (impact, urgency, priority) and two in B (impact, priority); A's tighter set is kept, both hold on the seed, and it is written with the row's key as anchor as B had it. disagreement: form: the SLA_008 stay has empty cells in A and sla_def_id in B; B's form is kept because the cell names what the count tests. Acting user USER_001 is an active admin (full CRUD), so nothing in the policy blocks the update. Both passes read 'update the necessary details' as the two consequences the policy derives from a changed impact (priority by the 3.1 matrix, SLA alignment by section 6); the caller's narrative (pending documents, extended deadline) is not turned into a work-note requirement because the request never asks for one and the tool list has no work-note tool.
revised: the SLA_008 stay's cells are now empty: its selector already fixes sla_def_id = 'SLA_008', so repeating that column in cells restated the selector rather than adding a predicate; its sql and count are unchanged.
